messages:
Alex: Quick heads-up: I'm going to migrate a TF module namespace from modules/network -> modules/core-networking. It affects provider sources and some secret paths. Planning to do a lockfile regen + a one-off terraform state mv job. Want a sanity check before I open the PR.
Priya: State migration plan? Are you doing terraform state mv or re-importing resources? :thinking_face: 
Alex: Plan is terraform state mv. Steps: 1) tiny PR that only renames module paths (no resource attr changes); 2) run a one-off job that does `terraform state mv` to move state entries; 3) regen providers lockfile (multi-arch) and run CI plan.
Matt: Ok. Couple of cautions: if provider source/version changes you can hit plugin/lockfile issues. Make sure the provider plugin used in the migration runner matches the one in the lockfile. Also consider pinning the provider at module level. Example: 
```
required_providers {
  aws = {
    source = "hashicorp/aws"
    version = "~> 5.4"
  }
}
```
Sam: Also note: the old networking module writes a Vault secret at `secret/data/network/cluster` but the new module reads `secret/data/core/network/cluster`. We need a secrets wiring plan (copy-or-migrate) or update consumers.
Alex: Good catch. I prefer copy-first: run `vault kv get` + `vault kv put` into the new path, verify consumers, then delete old key. We can include a small script in scripts/vault/copy-network-secret.sh.
infra-bot: CI: plan (infra/main) — FAILED — providers lockfile mismatch in modules/network (job 9127). :warning:
Priya: If lockfile mismatch is blocking, regenerate with `terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64 -platform=linux_arm64` using the same terraform binary version as CI.
Matt: Also ensure the migration runner uses the same terraform binary version as the state was created with. If checksums differ across platforms you can still run state mv, but `terraform plan` will fail until lockfile matches.
Alex: I'll pin the terraform version in the PR and add a GitHub Action job to run lockfile regen + `terraform plan` in a dry-run workspace. I'll open a PR and link it here.
Alex: Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4852 — includes module rename, provider pins, and a migration script at scripts/terraform/state-move.sh. Assigning @Matt and @Priya for review.
Sam: Can you paste the state-move.sh?
Alex: snippet pasted below: 
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
# expects TF_BACKEND_CONFIG and creds in env
cd infra/environments/prod
terraform init -backend-config="${TF_BACKEND_CONFIG}"
# move one example resource (expand as needed)
terraform state mv 'module.network.module.subnet.aws_subnet.this[0]' 'module.core_networking.module.subnet.aws_subnet.this[0]'
```
Priya: Suggestion: wrap the state mv in a dry-run toggle and capture stdout/stderr to a temp S3/GCS path for audit. Also add a maintenance window note and manual approval step.
Matt: I'll review tonight. Please include rollback steps in the runbook (how to restore old state snapshot and revert the module path if something goes wrong). Otherwise I'm +1 for the approach if CI is green and secrets are migrated.
Alex: Thanks — I'll add the runbook note, include multi-arch lockfile regen, and schedule the one-off job in the infra runbook. Will ping when CI passes. :eyes:
